### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **68** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/verify/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**15** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via keyId (symbol, a field of class ObjectExpiry))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class), archive.keep (literal, a string literal in archiveObject; a string literal in policy), expireAfter (literal, a string literal in reapSealed), maxAge (literal, a string literal in reapSealed), new_value (literal, a string literal in lifecycle), old_value (literal, a string literal in lifecycle), retention.maxAge (literal, a string literal in policy; a string literal in reapSealed))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via new_value (literal, a string literal in lifecycle), old_value (literal, a string literal in lifecycle))_
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via maxAge (literal, a string literal in reapSealed))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx`  _(via keyId (symbol, a field of class ObjectExpiry))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), new_value (literal, a string literal in lifecycle), old_value (literal, a string literal in lifecycle))_
- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via keyId (symbol, a field of class ObjectExpiry))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/verify/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **28** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `89195c3d728ee20147506da3ebce24e5e30dc1d1` — the merge of head `46e272ed4599332945e9a7e0709e08f08408f8aa` into base `41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 89195c3d728ee20147506da3ebce24e5e30dc1d1 && git checkout 89195c3d728ee20147506da3ebce24e5e30dc1d1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e 46e272ed4599332945e9a7e0709e08f08408f8aa && git checkout -B drift-repro 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e && git merge --no-ff 46e272ed4599332945e9a7e0709e08f08408f8aa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4deab949980d45dd8a860ca86b187b4c38379691`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/expiry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/verifier.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts, packages/verify/src/harness.ts

Inputs: card #31908 (body and all 62 comments), PR #37605 (body, 28 files, net diff against merge base `061e3422`), ADR-0154 as on the head, and the head's check-runs, read 2026-11-26T16:48Z: 62 success, 12 skipped, none failed or pending. The rest of the diff (tests, the changeset's prose, the three docs pages, the census page, `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, `packages/verify/vitest.config.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `sys_audit_log` declares `seal: { valueFields: ['old_value', 'new_value', 'metadata'] }`. Right: ADR-0154 D10's value, word for word; the chain column is the default.
2. Every project's `os audit verify` now reports `sealed: true` with `sys_audit_log` in `objects`, and exits 2 when the `archive` datasource the ledger names is declared and not reachable. Right (D9, D10).
3. `LifecycleService.registerSealedExpiry` and the exported types `LifecycleSealedExpiry`, `LifecycleSealedExpiryRequest`, `LifecycleSealedExpiryRun`. Right as a widening (D8, "a seam beside `registerReapGuard`"). The name is not the one slice plan 6759503769 ruled; see ③.
4. `LifecycleSweepEntry.policy` gains `'expiry'` and `report.skipped` gains the reason `seal-expiry-pending`. Right, a widening of a published report shape; the declaration line does not name it.
5. On an object declaring `lifecycle.seal`, `retention.maxAge`, `ttl.expireAfter` and `archive.keep` no longer delete by a row cutoff. Right against D8. It is a changed meaning of authored keys, which the declaration reads as `none`: wrong, see ② S2.
6. A tenant-scoped `retention_overrides` window is not applied to a sealed object with no archive. Wrong as built, see ④ S1; and a narrowing the declaration does not carry.
7. With no sealed expiry registered the rows are kept, including the cold `archive.keep` prune of `sys_audit_log` on a deployment whose `AuditPlugin` has no crypto provider. Right (D8's seam bullet), and stated.
8. `os migrate audit-* --apply` needs `--sealer-stopped` on SQLite and Turso on every deployment, and takes the audit seal lock on Postgres and MySQL on every deployment. Ruled; declared wrong, see ② M2.
9. The verifier's third sealed-window arm: more rows read `late` unsealed and `os audit verify` exits 1 where it exited 0. Right: seat ruling 6885452378 and D3 as amended, as written.
10. `verifyAuditLedger` (a root export) needs `archive` passed where the datasource `sys_audit_log` archives to is not connected. Follows from 1; a narrowing for a library caller, stated in the PR body only.
11. The verify harness hands `harnessCryptoProvider()` to an `AuditPlugin` it mounts, on all three mount paths, through `adoptHostCryptoProvider`. Right: ruling 6884540128 item 4.
12. The sealer's head and floor fall back to the last expiry when no checkpoint is left. Right (D8).
13. The `lifecycle.seal` `.describe()` sentence: prose only, no accept-set change, the reference page regenerated.

### ② Semver level

The changeset moves `plugin-audit`, `objectql`, `verify` and `spec` at `patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The widening half is true. Two things are not.

M2 (must-fix) — the declaration carries no narrowing, and this diff narrows. This card's own precedent is changeset `35c9a30` (#33675): it declared the same refusal `yes (narrowing)` under a `**BREAKING**` banner with an ADR-0087 marker, and bounded it with "No object declares `lifecycle.seal` by default, so a deployment that did not opt in sees no change". This diff is the change that opts every deployment in. Narrowed here:
- `os migrate audit-key-material`, `audit-mail-bodies`, `audit-metadata-bodies` and `audit-side-copies` with `--apply` on SQLite or Turso are refused without `--sealer-stopped` on every deployment. Their object lists name `sys_audit_log` statically and `holdAuditSealLock` reads `lifecycle.seal` off the registry, so the refusal does not depend on whether a row needs rewriting.
- On Postgres and MySQL the same runs now take the audit seal lock on every deployment, wait up to ten minutes for a sealer pass, then refuse. The changeset's "as before" holds only for a deployment that had opted in.
- `os audit verify` exits 1 on rows the new arm reads `late` unsealed (item 9).
- `verifyAuditLedger` without `archive` (item 10).
- The tenant-scoped window (item 6).
Owed on both carriers: the `(narrowing)` arm beside the widening, the BREAKING banner with the one-line fix for each item, the ADR-0087 disposition marker, and the `Skills-docs:` line the arm brings. The changeset's bullet on `--sealer-stopped` is true as far as it goes; it is the banner and the arm that are missing.

S2 (should-fix) — `Metadata-protocol: none` reads the diff as a platform object's declaration only. The diff also changes what `retention`, `ttl` and `archive.keep` mean beside `seal` on any author's object (item 5), and rewrites the key's own `.describe()` to say so. AGENTS.md names a changed meaning `semantic`, and the shipped changelogs use `semantic` for runtime changes of this kind. `semantic` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, so the level does not match either. The seat rules the kind on the card; if it keeps `none`, the ruling says why item 5 is not a changed meaning.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Sealed by default, so `--sealer-stopped` on every SQLite and Turso deployment.** Covered: D10 rules the default, D3 as amended (B) and seat ruling 6885005594 item 2 rule the flag for any object declaring `lifecycle.seal`, and slice plan 6759503769 put the default in this slice. Stated true in the changeset. Maintainer's decision: none is owed on the rule itself. What is owed is M2, the dev's to fix. It goes to the maintainer only if the seat contests that M2 is a narrowing, because 18.6.0 told operators a deployment that did not opt in would see no change.
- Operator pages outside this diff, for the lane seat: `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` is on the claimed surface and untouched; its `os migrate audit-*` section says only "Run them with the server stopped" and never names the flag or the lock. `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` ties the flag to "where an app declares `lifecycle.seal`". Both are false for a default deployment once this lands.
- Carrier: cloud. Turso environments meet the refusal on their next `os migrate audit-*` run, and a host that passes no crypto provider to `AuditPlugin` now keeps `sys_audit_log` past `archive.keep` and reports hourly at `error`.
- **No crypto provider: rows kept, said once at `warn`.** Answered: right. D8 rules that a missing amendment keeps the rows, and the sealer's own `error` line carries the durability half.
- **A tenant-scoped override does not apply to a sealed object.** Named for this review by amendment 7195525477; no ruling covers it. S1 below. It needs a ruling of record: the seat's, and the maintainer's if the ruling would let a chain expire under a window shorter than the one configured for it.
- **The cutoff aligned down to a UTC day, and 10,000 rows a sweep.** Escalated to the seat. D8 states the extra retention as "at most one window plus the late horizon" and the Consequences line repeats it; the build adds up to one day, and a backlog adds more. The direction is safe and verification still honours the amendment. Under Prime Directive 13 the bound changes by a record: a seat ruling on the card and an add-only ADR-0154 note in its own governed PR, as #33489 did for the three rulings before it. The budget is also per object across all chains, where the Archiver bound it cites is per pass.
- **The seam's name.** Slice plan 6759503769 ruled `registerExpiryPrefix`; the diff ships `registerSealedExpiry` and no later ruling renames it. The seat confirms the name on the card before it is published.
- **File surface.** `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx` and the four `os migrate` integration files are in the diff and in no claim line (7193045552, 7193137455, 7195525477). An amendment is owed; the lane seat's.
- **The skills sentence.** `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` keeps "Not built yet ... the sweeper still deletes sealed rows" from this merge until the second PR, and this PR's closing keyword closes the card first. The seat's call; its own example there (`retention` beside `seal`, no archive) is the shape S1 is about.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The chain walk, the run walk and the head reads push their filter, order and limit down. The id lists of `runOf` and `deleteSealedRows` are the row ids a checkpoint's signed body carries, which D8 makes the unit of deletion, and the per-row engine delete is `batchedReap`'s, for the guards.
- Ruling 6885452378 item 6 (the notice and the no-later-window case) is deferred by the ruling itself.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`.** One `.describe()` sentence. It holds against D8 and D10 and against its first consumer, `sys_audit_log`: `archive.keep` expires by whole checkpoints through the seam, and without a registered expiry the sweeper keeps the rows. No shape change.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts`.** Holds: D10's value, class `audit`, no `onlyWhen`, `archive.after` equal to `retention.maxAge`.

**`packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts`.** The routing holds against D8: an archiving sealed object expires on `keep` alone, on both stores, by id; any other sealed object expires through its `ttl` and `retention` legs; rows go before `complete()`; an unfinished run is not completed; a throwing plan deletes nothing; no expiry means no delete.

S1 (should-fix) — `reapSealed` drops a tenant-scoped window and expires every chain under the global one. On `main` that window was applied to a sealed object like any other (`reap`, `tenantWindowsFor`). Where a tenant's window is longer than the global one, its rows are now expired earlier than the operator configured, after one `warn`. That is a delete, on an audit-class object, and it contradicts the PR's own rule that anything off keeps rows. The stated reason, one signed policy value per chain, does not force it: by default a chain is one organization's, and each chain's amendment carries its own policy value. The seat rules the shape (a per-chain value, or the longest window as the one value); either way a chain is never expired under a window shorter than the one configured for it. `sys_audit_log` itself is not affected: it archives, and `keep` has no override.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/expiry.ts`.** The fresh run holds against D8 sentence by sentence: it starts at the first remaining sequence, which must follow the last admitted expiry; takes consecutive checkpoints whose windows ended by the cutoff; admits each; signs and stores the amendment before it answers; carries the last removed digest, the policy and its value; resumes a stored range before it signs another.

M1 (must-fix) — `expiry.ts`. One finding in a security-adjacent path. Its statement is withheld from this record and handed to the seat off the public thread, as report 6821958333 did. The delta record closes it by id.

S3 (should-fix) — the resumed range is read with no `orderBy`, so `complete()` removes its checkpoints in driver order. `sealer.ts` says of `expire` that the pass's locks keep a sealer pass from reading a chain head the expiry is moving, but `complete()` runs after `expire` has released them. What keeps a concurrent pass's head right is that the newest checkpoint goes last and the expiry fallback then answers the same head, which is true by construction only in the fresh run. Read the resumed range ascending by `sequence`, and make the sentence name what protects the head.

**`sealer.ts`, `audit-plugin.ts`.** `expire` holds: both locks around planning and signing, no run while either is held, a throw with no crypto or signer, the memo only for a plan that found nothing. The head and floor fallbacks hold against D8. Registration only with a crypto provider, and its removal on `destroy()`, hold.

**`verifier.ts`.** The arm is ruling 6885452378 item 1 as written, and D3's amended bullet says the same.

**`packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`.** Hold: the one harness provider on all three mount paths, never a bare provider, an instance with its own provider left alone; the three types exported.

Nits:
- n1 — the `.describe()` sentence and `objects.mdx` do not say what a tenant-scoped window or the day alignment does on a sealed object; they follow S1's ruling.
- n2 — `expiry.ts`'s header says rows stay at most one day past their policy on top of D8's bound; the row budget can add more.
- n3 — on the stores path `deleteSealedRows` answers that every row is gone once `bulkDelete` did not throw, and asks `bulkDelete` of a cold driver the boot checked for `upsert` only (the old prune guarded `deleteMany`). A cold driver without it fails each sweep after the amendment is signed: loud, and it keeps the rows.

**VERDICT: FAIL**
